TABLE.LABEL: Table
TABLE.TOOLTIP: Raw rows — every record shown as-is.
TABLE.NOTE: Shows raw rows — every record exactly as it's stored, no grouping or aggregation. Best for inspecting source data.

VERTICAL_BAR.LABEL: Bar
VERTICAL_BAR.NOTE: Compares one or more measures across a single dimension. Put the category on the columns shelf and an aggregated measure (sum, count, avg…) on the rows shelf.

HORIZONTAL_BAR.LABEL: H-Bar
HORIZONTAL_BAR.TOOLTIP: Bars laid out horizontally — better for long category names.
HORIZONTAL_BAR.NOTE: Horizontal bars — same data as Bar, but easier to read when category labels are long.

LINE.LABEL: Line
LINE.NOTE: Shows how a measure trends across an ordered dimension — usually a date. Put the time field on the columns shelf and the measure on the rows shelf. Add a field to Marks → Color for multiple lines.

AREA.LABEL: Area
AREA.TOOLTIP: Line chart with the area below filled in.
AREA.NOTE: Same shape as Line, with the area under the curve filled in to emphasise volume over time.

DONUT.LABEL: Donut
DONUT.TOOLTIP: Share of a total with a hollow center.
DONUT.NOTE: A pie with a hole — same use as Pie. The center can show the grand total.

PIE.LABEL: Pie
PIE.TOOLTIP: Share of a total across a dimension.
PIE.NOTE: Shows each category's share of a total. Best with a small number of categories (5–7). For many categories, a Bar chart is easier to read.

KPI.LABEL: KPI
KPI.NOTE: A single aggregated number — sum / count / avg / max / min of one measure. No dimension needed. Use it on the dashboard for headline metrics.

TOUR.WELCOME_DESC: Build your own report by choosing fields, shaping them on shelves, and picking how to visualise the result. This quick tour points out each part — use ← / → or the buttons, and Esc to exit.
TOUR.STEP1_DESC: Pick your data source at the top, then browse its fields here. Double-click a field or drag it onto a shelf to add it to the report.
TOUR.STEP2_DESC: This bar shows/hides the shelves area where you arrange fields. It stays open while you build.
TOUR.STEP3_DESC: Drop fields onto Columns and Rows to structure the report, and onto Filters to limit the data. Aggregations (sum, count, …) live on each field.
TOUR.STEP4_DESC: Encode extra meaning: set a Color field, and toggle data labels. For charts this controls how series are coloured.
TOUR.STEP5_DESC: Create your own computed columns (e.g. margin = price − cost) to use like any other field.
TOUR.STEP6_DESC: Switch between a Table and chart types (bar, line, pie, …). Hover a type to see when to use it.
TOUR.STEP7_DESC: Fetch the latest data for your current setup. Turn on Auto-refresh in Settings to run as you edit.
TOUR.STEP8_DESC: Your report renders here. In table view, click a column header to sort (fetched from the server) and reorder columns by dragging.
TOUR.STEP9_DESC: Large tables are paged — step through pages and change the page size without loading everything at once.
TOUR.STEP10_DESC: A report can hold multiple sheets (e.g. a table and a chart of the same data). Add, rename and switch between them here.
TOUR.STEP11_DESC: Save your report. Saved reports appear under the Custom Report tab in Reports.
TOUR.STEP12_DESC: Once saved, open Customize Dashboard → Available Widgets → the “Custom” filter, and drop your report onto the dashboard as a live widget — with its own records limit, sort and filters. You're all set! 🎉
